01 / THE PRACTICE

More intention.
At every turn.

Editorial Studio gives your coding agent a repeatable editorial process. It asks what matters, develops two creative directions and keeps you involved at the decisions that shape the publication.

From brief to final read.

SIX STEPS. ONE COHERENT ISSUE.

THE EDITORIAL PROMISE

Know what this
publication is for.

Define the subject, purpose and audience. Set the tone, share a reference or choose no example. The brief becomes the standard for every decision that follows.

The editorial skill

Instructions and references that guide your coding agent through planning, editing, brand development, photography storytelling and whole-issue review.

  • Editorial promise, story mix & flatplan
  • Reusable brand sheet & issue variations
  • Headlines, captions & evidence checks

B

The local dashboard

A separate Python application for organising features, reviewing images and exporting PDFs. Runs on your own device.

  • Two baseline visual themes
  • Image provenance & exact-asset approval
  • PDF progress indicator & estimated time
  • Preflight, image & hyperlink audits
Set up the dashboard ↗
THE CURRENT CANVAS

A4 portrait. Up to 12 magazine feature pages or 3 onepager features. RGB PDF output. High-end custom proof spreads are a separate, explicitly approved phase. No claim of CMYK, bleed or press-ready certification.

PUBLIC SOURCE / v0.4.0

Choose one
installation route.

The skill adds instructions and references. It does not install Python dependencies or a hosted application.

Open GitHub repository ↗

Installing the skill does not upload publications. Content you share with your AI tool follows that provider's settings and terms.

  1. Open Codex

    Use the bundled Skill Installer with the prompt below. The source is public; no GitHub invitation or private-repository token is required for the standard download.

  2. Paste this into Codex

    $skill-installer install https://github.com/hndrk-020/editorial-studio/tree/main/.agents/skills/editorial-studio

    The bundled installer normally uses ~/.codex/skills. It refuses to overwrite an existing skill folder; back up local edits before a deliberate update.

  3. Check that Codex can load it

    Start a new turn; restart Codex if needed. Use the verification prompt below and check the reported skill path.

  1. Download and extract the source

    Open the public repository, choose Code → Download ZIP on main, then Extract All. Do not run scripts inside the ZIP preview.

  2. Run the installer

    Double-click install_codex_skill_windows.cmd. It copies the full skill to %USERPROFILE%\.agents\skills\editorial-studio. No administrator access or Python is needed for this copy.

    Existing installation? Back it up before approving replacement. The script overlays files; it does not remove obsolete files.

  3. Verify the files and discovery

    Test-Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.agents\skills\editorial-studio\SKILL.md"

    Run this in PowerShell. Expect True, then start a new Codex turn and use the prompt below to verify loading.

VERIFY THE SKILL / CODEX EXAMPLE
$editorial-studio Confirm you can load the skill and its editorial planning and brand system references. Tell me the loaded SKILL.md path. Do not start a publication yet.
PDF export / Set up the local application+

To use this project's PDF renderer, keep the complete repository and install Python 3.11 or newer. The skill alone does not include the application. The first launch requires internet to install dependencies.

Windows

Double-click run_windows.cmd in the extracted repository. To check readiness without installing anything, open PowerShell in that folder:

.\run_windows.cmd --check

macOS & Linux

bash run_mac_linux.sh

Check readiness without downloading or starting the app:

bash run_mac_linux.sh --check

The readiness check lists missing prerequisites and changes no files. A successful check verifies the local files and dependencies; AI-tool discovery and the final PDF still need their own checks. Open the complete app setup guide ↗

Open http://127.0.0.1:8765. Keep the terminal running; Ctrl+C stops the application. Keep it on localhost. The dashboard and PDF export run locally. Content you share with your AI tool is handled under that provider's settings and terms.

Already installed? Update without losing local edits.+

Keep one intended user-wide copy. The Windows installer uses ~/.agents/skills; the bundled Skill Installer normally uses ~/.codex/skills. A project-local copy can also exist. Ask Codex for the loaded path before changing anything.

Back up the whole existing skill folder outside active skill directories. Update the complete folder, including references. Preserve local changes and verify loading again.

04 / YOUR FIRST BRIEF — CODEX EXAMPLE

Bring a subject.
Keep your point of view.

$editorial-studio Help me create a one-page product introduction for prospective customers. Ask about my product, audience, purpose, desired style and an inspiration URL or no example. Present two distinct creative directions before production. Use only verified facts and approved imagery; never invent customer results. Confirm the separate local PDF application is ready before export.

This example uses Codex syntax. In other tools, ask the agent to load Editorial Studio and confirm its invocation method. You approve the direction and exact images; the exported PDF still needs a visual review.

BUILT WITH BOUNDARIES

Real sources.
Explicit approvals.

Photography is researched and reviewed by a person. Provenance and rights evidence are recorded; approval fields do not prove a licence. Missing or unapproved images block export.

Reviewed.
Still accountable.

The release review recorded 41 passing Linux tests and 40 passes with one platform-specific skip on native Windows. Windows/Ubuntu CI also passed. A dependency scan found no known advisories at review time. This is not a security certification.
